sources.role: metric formula, worked example, submission format (ground truth for metric.py and submission_io.py)
verified_facts: DTI formula: TP_w/(TP_w+alpha*FP_w+beta*FN_w)
triangular kernel k(d)=max(1-d/R,0), R=300m=3px at 100m
alpha=0.2, beta=0.8 fixed for this competition
worked example: TP_w=3.00, FP_w=1.89, FN_w=2.00 -> DTI=0.60
submission must be single-band float32 GeoTIFF, EPSG:32611, 100m, values in [0,1], same bounds as training data, outside-bounds must be null/NaN

17 feature categories listed: conductivity+depth, detrended elevation+slope, dilatation/shear/2nd-invariant strain, isostatic gravity+slope, RTP magnetics, TMI, vertical/horizontal slope of TMI, crustal magnetic source depth, earthquake density
GeoDAWN = USGS EarthMRI aeromagnetic+aeroradiometric survey, coordinated with 3DEP lidar
cites Matteo et al. 2021 JGR Solid Earth doi:10.1029/2020JB021269 and Hermant et al. 2025 Stanford Geothermal Workshop

sources.role: organizer-linked baseline (U-Net, Prof. John Lipor, Portland State)
verified_facts: cloned directly (github.com is in this sandbox's allowed host list); README and notebook read in full
loads data/numeric_features.tif and data/labels.tif via rasterio
treats values < -1e38 as nodata -> NaN (the exact sentinel our submission_io.py strips)
normalizes each channel to [0,1] with nanmin/nanmax, trains a 5-iteration Monte-Carlo cross-validated resnet18 U-Net with segmentation_models_pytorch, TverskyLoss(alpha=0.2, beta=0.8, mode='binary')
writes the prediction with the fault-label raster's own CRS/transform (rasterio.open(..., crs=fault_dataset.crs, transform=fault_dataset.transform))
known USGS/INGENIOUS fault pixels are masked/excluded from scoring in BOTH Phase 1 and Phase 2, identical to the provided training fault labels
the mask is PIXEL-EXACT, not buffered
a predicted pixel near (but not on) a known fault is NOT protected: it is fully penalized against the new-fault ground truth if that ground truth is far away
a new-fault ground-truth pixel CAN sit within 300 m of a known fault (e.g. splays, tip extensions, corrections to existing traces are an explicit target of the competition)
